entries.title: Shell-mediated Process launch from untrusted Swift values
source_cues: untrusted input reaches a Process launch configuration
a shell command string is assembled before launching a process
sink_cues: Process launches /bin/sh or another interpreter with -c and attacker-influenced text
language_pitfalls: Foundation.Process arguments are argv elements and do not invoke a shell by themselves.
Injection risk arises when the selected executable is a shell/interpreter or arguments are reinterpreted by a child command.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Trace values into executableURL and every arguments element.
Determine whether a shell/interpreter is launched; compare argv-based and shell-string behavior.

entries.title: Out-of-bounds write through Swift unsafe buffers or C interop
source_cues: Swift code passes a pointer and length across a C ABI boundary
sink_cues: UnsafeMutablePointer/UnsafeMutableBufferPointer subscripts, pointer arithmetic, and raw-memory writes
C functions receiving Swift buffer baseAddress/count pairs
language_pitfalls: Ordinary Array subscripting performs bounds checks; focus on unsafe buffers, raw pointers, and imported C contracts.
withUnsafeBytes pointer lifetime ends at closure exit; do not retain the pointer.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Trace count/capacity conversions and pointer arithmetic to the write.
Check lifetime scope and imported C function length contract; use sanitizers where available.

entries.title: Dangling Swift/C object reference across ARC or Unmanaged lifetime boundary
source_cues: Unmanaged/passRetained/passUnretained or a C callback retains a reference
object lifetime ends while an unsafe pointer/callback remains reachable
sink_cues: C/Objective-C callback or stored opaque pointer dereferences after owner release
language_pitfalls: ARC-managed strong references normally prevent UAF; examine Unmanaged, unsafe pointers, bridging, and foreign callbacks.
Retain-count imbalance may cause leaks or premature release; distinguish the actual failure mode.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Map retain/release ownership across the Swift/Objective-C/C boundary.
Verify callback cancellation and owner lifetime with a controlled reproducer.

entries.title: Out-of-bounds read through Swift unsafe buffer or imported C pointer
source_cues: untrusted count/index reaches UnsafeBufferPointer or raw pointer access
a Swift buffer and count are passed to a C reader
sink_cues: unsafe buffer subscript and pointer advanced(by:)
C functions reading beyond the supplied pointer/count contract
language_pitfalls: Ordinary Collection subscripts are bounds checked; focus on unsafe APIs and FFI contracts.
Validate integer narrowing and element-count multiplication before constructing buffer views.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Trace length units, integer casts, and pointer offsets to the read.
Check initialized count and foreign function contract; use sanitizers where available.

entries.title: Missing authorization on a Swift server route or privileged operation
source_cues: a Vapor/NIO request reaches a sensitive operation
route registration or middleware determines whether a principal is required
sink_cues: database, filesystem, or administrative operations reachable from a request
language_pitfalls: Swift access control and type visibility are not request authorization.
A route group or middleware declaration is not effective unless it dominates every alias and registration path.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Enumerate route registrations, groups, middleware order, and aliases.
Test anonymous and least-privileged requests against the sensitive operation.

entries.title: Incorrect principal/resource authorization in a Swift server handler
source_cues: request principal and resource/role identifiers are checked in separate code paths
authorization result is derived from a route parameter or decoded request value
sink_cues: Vapor/NIO route handlers and service methods
resource read/write after a role, owner, or tenant comparison
language_pitfalls: Authentication proves identity, not permission for the selected object or action.
Check middleware and service-layer policy consistency across aliases.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Trace the authenticated principal and selected resource through the exact policy branch.
Compare owner, cross-tenant, and wrong-role controls.

entries.title: Swift server object lookup uses a request-controlled key without ownership scoping
source_cues: route/query/body identifier selects a server-side object
authenticated principal or tenant is available separately
sink_cues: Vapor route parameters and ORM/repository lookups
resource mutation/read after lookup by a request-controlled key
language_pitfalls: UUIDs and opaque identifiers do not establish ownership.
Authorization must cover nested, batch, and alternate route lookups.
counterevidence: Safe high-level Swift collection access retains runtime bounds checks.
The foreign pointer contract and owner lifetime are validated at the boundary.
verification_steps: Trace request identifiers into reads and writes and inspect query tenant/owner constraints.
Test same-tenant and cross-tenant principals against the same object key.
